passages.provision_quote: In an action against a defendant who developed, modified, or used artificial intelligence that is alleged to have caused a harm to the plaintiff, it shall not be a defense, and the defendant may not assert, that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff.
passages.note: Single-subject Civil Code bill she authored, chaptered 2025, whose only operative section bars the AI-autonomy defense for defendants who developed AI.

rows.reasoning: Krell authored AB 316 (2025-2026), a single-subject Civil Code act whose operative section provides that in an action against a defendant "who developed, modified, or used artificial intelligence that is alleged to have caused a harm to the plaintiff, it shall not be a defense" that the AI "autonomously caused the harm". That keeps the party who built the system answerable in law for the harm it causes, matching the rung "Hold AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm" clause for clause: legal responsibility, on a defendant class that expressly includes developers, for harm the system caused. It requires no pre-use safety testing and no government approval, so the rungs on either side of it are excluded by the bill's own text.
